modality_prompt:
Use raw RGB together with the annotated view and detection list to judge the scene. Detections may be wrong or incomplete; missing detections do not mean absence. Verify person detections in RGB before treating them as civilians; robots or equipment may be mislabeled. The detector also checks fire extinguisher and robot dog (including nozzle/quadruped aliases); strongly overlapping person/equipment masks may be filtered before annotation and target creation. This visual conflict filter is heuristic, not confirmed civilian identity; unmatched or ambiguous detections still require RGB verification. During-action captures provide raw RGB only. Ending surroundings provide raw RGB followed by an annotated image only when annotation_available is true; otherwise only raw RGB is sent. The detection list remains available for both.
The label list distinguishes category=object/person/fire and includes label, confidence, pixel bbox_xyxy and grounding_available. Pixel boxes use the original RGB dimensions. Person labels do not establish NPC identity, health or a confirmed pose. A fire's attached_to is a same-frame visual association with an object/person target_ref, not an Oracle burning-state confirmation. When grounded, fire uses the attached target's coordinate (grounding_source=attached_target), not flame depth. An unknown attachment remains null. Objects and people use grounding_source=mask_depth when grounded. For targets seen only in RGB or without valid grounding, use further observation or room/relative navigation as needed. Entity actions require an exact target_ref with grounding_available=true from the current ending surroundings batch; route frames and memory describe history, not executable targets. If a remembered fire or object is absent or ungrounded in the latest surroundings, reobserve or approach using room/relative navigation before acting. Never reuse an old frame reference, invent references or coordinates. Matching class labels across frames do not establish identity. The executor resolves coordinates. Treat precise health as unknown unless explicitly reported.
Frames follow during_action, then surroundings; use their timestamps to distinguish route history from the ending observation. Visual suppression has no automatic fire-state verification: after a command executes, its effect report is unknown. An execution failure or rejected target means suppression was not confirmed to run; an unknown visual effect must not be interpreted as successful spraying or extinguishing. Interpret the images as visual evidence without treating them as a programmatic fire_extinguished confirmation.
Follower feedback and following_npcs use system-supplied civilian names; newly_following_npcs identifies additions to the prior report.
